patch_description: Instead of stochastic Metropolis annealing, this uses analytic gradient ascent on a smooth soft-minimum surrogate: weights w_t = softmax(-alpha * area_t) over all 286 triangles, with exact analytic gradients of the signed triangle areas (grad wrt vertex v = 0.5*w*sign*R(p_u - p_w)). A continuation schedule increases alpha over time so the surrogate tightens from "raise the average small triangles" to "raise the true minimum", sharpening the basin of attraction without random-walk noise. A per-restart adaptive step controller (grow 1.05 on improvement, shrink 0.7 on regression) replaces fixed cooling ladders. Periodic rescaling to unit hull area makes the optimized quantity equal to the normalized score directly. Multi-start over structured inits, followed by a short targeted greedy polish on the K smallest triangles to squeeze the exact minimum. This should outperform annealing because every step follows the exact gradient direction of the binding constraint set rather than relying on random proposals, converging in fewer, better-directed iterations.
